concepts.title: Reference combination
concepts.instruction: Draw the 60 mm base and 30 mm top frustum with 40 mm height. Place the R20 hemisphere centrally with its flat face upwards.

concepts.title: Frustum base oval
concepts.instruction: Construct the 60 mm isometric rhombus and four-centre base oval.

concepts.title: Frustum top oval
concepts.instruction: Set off the 40 mm vertical axis and construct the 30 mm top rhombus and oval.

concepts.title: Frustum sides
concepts.instruction: Draw the two visible common tangent generators between base and top ovals.

concepts.title: Hemisphere centre and rim
concepts.instruction: From the top centre/contact point raise the hemisphere centre by 20 mm and construct the horizontal 40 mm circular rim as an isometric oval.

concepts.title: Hemisphere curved boundary
concepts.instruction: Use the enlarged sphere silhouette radius sqrt(3/2) × 20 ≈ 24.49 mm (source: 1.22 R20) for the visible lower curved outline, meeting the rim as shown.

concepts.title: Complete combination
concepts.instruction: Retain the construction boxes, centre O, tangent lines and given dimensions.

notes: The PDF scale and question text visibly overlap at top right; do not infer lost dimensions from that overlap. A separate statement panel can improve readability while the drawing coordinates remain unchanged.
The hemisphere rests at its lowest pole on the centre of the frustum top. Its equatorial flat face is 20 mm above that contact level; do not seat the flat face on the frustum.
The upper oval represents the flat circular face, while the circular silhouette arc represents the curved spherical surface. They are different curves and must not both be drawn as the same ellipse.
